Pros
+ Among the cutest and sexiest voice acting I have seen in the father and daughter pair, the accents is amazing lol.
+ Traditional hand drawn inspired background and graphics, the people animation are simpler 2D shaders but still nicely drawn and pleasing.
+ No crazy unsolvable puzzles, didn't have to use a hint or solution guide. Most are quite logical or limited in environmental interaction for you to figure it out.
+ While not the best storyline, its still entertaining enough though a lot has been left unsaid about the world and world building.
+ Cute side characters, here's to you dog, caterpillar and giant water monster.
+ Nostalgic return to old school adventure games for those missing it.
+ The black cat, cutest thing in the world (i own one so this tugs at my heartstrings seriously).

Cons
- The game puzzles and mechanics are simple and straightforward.
- It's a short game and by short its even poked fun at it with a speed run achievement of an hour.
- The villain, not the most inspiring and the voice acting, meeerrr, sadly no.

PROS:
1. The art is just... on another level! 2D, traditionally drawn characters with fluid Disney-esque animation, stunning backgrounds, and just... WOW! There was so much detail - you would see a hand-drawn animation of a rat running on the foreground, for no other reason then to contribute to the atmosphere. My eyes were having a feast just watching the funny expressions of the characters (the CAT) or the details in the backgrounds! I cannot stress enough how impressed I was with the animation!
2. The characters, on top of being perfectly animated and highly expressive, were enjoyable to follow. No, I can't say there was a lot of depth and complexity in terms of the story, but I was never bored, and the funny situations that both protagonists stumbled into kept me entertained.
3. Of course, I will soon move on to CONS, but before I do, I want to say that this game sure wasn't perfect, but it felt very personal. You can tell it was done with passion and love, and I hope to see more games like that.

CONS:
1. The BIGGEST one was BUGS! I didn't see anyone else complain about this, so it could be just me, but there were several occasions. For example, when I loaded a saved game, the mouse would disappear and I wouldn't be able to do anything (I had to reload the save a few times until it started working). Another example: I kept jumping back and forward on the lilly pads (just clicking aggressively with the mouse until it stopped). Fortunately, both of these were fixable, and I didn't have to restart the game.
2. The puzzles were divided into three types: perfectly challenging, childish, or ridiculously convoluted. I didn't know there was a hint system, so I had to use a walkthrough 3–4 times when I was stuck. Unfortunately, there were a few occasions where, even if I did find the solution by myself by mistake, it would seem so absurd that it would take me out of the immersion.
3. The game is super short. I actually had dinner while playing it and with the long breaks it took about 2.5 hours. I bought it for about €3, so of course I was't expecting anything lengthy. Just make sure you wait for the discounts, €13 is too much for 2 hours of gameplay in my personal opinion. 

I am happy to have The Little Acre in my Steam collection :)

It's a pretty game, but that's about as far as I can compliment it. The point & click genre demands an engaging story or interesting puzzles to hold the player's interest, but this game unfortunately fails to satisfy either of those requirements. Beyond the very first area of the game, puzzles don't get much more complex than interacting with at most four interactive elements all on a single screen. Without engaging puzzles, the only thing left is the story and well... it fails to gain any momentum. The game introduces characters pivotal to the plot without making any attempt to flesh them out whatsoever, and then suddenly ends unexpectedly as soon as what one would think is the 2nd act of the story, in a way that ties everything up so neatly I feel almost insulted.

Overall, there's barely an hour's worth of gameplay here, and at $18.50, that's an extremely steep asking price for a game with very little length and substance. I sadly have to say pass on this one.

The Little Acre is a charming point and click title with focus on the animation. It's a short title - I played it 3 times to get all achievements (around 4 hours).
The story, I feel, was the weakest point of the game. It kinda was there to motor everything but the exposure and just somewhat fast, rushed pacing felt off. All characters were just somewhat of a shell of something but still, they served their purpose.
With that in mind, you would have thought I wouldn't recommend the title. Yet, I came in for the artstyle mostly and stayed for it. The animation can be sometimes wonky but with a small production team, I understand why that was the case. The expression however, were so silly at times - ESPECIALLY Douglas the dog was my favourite with just broad range of emotions showing on the animal's face. I feel the focus was due to the game being in memory of an actual dog - and I found that quite lovely. 
The sound design was also okay, nothing really that will stay with me yet, it had brought charm here and there. I do feel the voice acting could use a bit of maybe more flare to it but as I said - I came for the art style and stayed for it.

I unfortunately do think that if you would want it, you should get it on a sale - as I did, which probably impacts my overall view of the game. But still, I do think people should give it a try and have a nice evening with it ;)

Купил я "The Little Acre" ещё в 2018 году на распродаже из-за привлекательного дизайна и хороших отзывов (не помню, сколько было тогда, но сейчас, на момент написания обзора, у этой игры 86% положительных отзывов), а сел за неё лишь в январе 2022 года. Увы, данная игра вызвала у меня [i][b]смешанные эмоции[/b][/i]. Что же не так с игрой?

Да, дизайн просто бомбезный: прям получаешь удовольствие от такой милой рисовки! Вдобавок, локации прорисованы очень даже хорошо... И всё, на этом достоинства игры заканчиваются.

А вот недостатков (или, скорее, недочётов) тут много:
[olist]
[*][b]Сюжет.[/b] Чего-то интересного из себя не представляет, но и не бесит. В общем, просто неплохая история.

[*][b]Квестовая составляющая.[/b] Вот тут она очень средне сделана, т.к. все загадки решаются очень легко и быстро, отчего удовольствия вообще не получаешь.

[*][b]Продолжительность.[/b] [u]2 часа на игру - слишком мало![/u] Тебе за это время не дают ни интересного сюжета, ни интересного геймплея, из-за чего каких-то ярких эмоций ты не получаешь.
[/olist]
По итогу, "The Little Acre" получился достаточно средним проектом, и какую-то однозначную оценку (чисто положительную или чисто отрицательную) сложно дать, т.к. с одной стороны, у игры достаточно недочётов, а с другой - каких-то прям отрицательных эмоций я не получил за время прохождения. Была бы возможность поставить игре среднюю оценку, я бы именно её и поставил бы, но увы, такой возможности в Steam нет, поэтому я решил написать именно положительный обзор из-за небольшого перевеса в виде прекраснейшего дизайна.

From a standard point-and-click adventure point of view, The Little Acre is underwhelming. My positive review comes with a heavy caveat. It's not challenging, long, or exceptionally funny, but it is incredibly endearing. I recommend it on the basis that it is a veritable pallet reset. 

It's almost too short in that it leaves a lot of questions unanswered and fails to develop some of the more endearing parts of itself. It's a movie that flies too fast and expects you to pick up the pieces. But. It's amusing enough that if you're looking for a quick point and click adventure jaunt, it won't matter too much. 

Worth a shot if you like point and click adventure. There's a lot of better games out there in this space, but this one is good if you're looking for something simple and quick with a little bit of heart.
